title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Tech-led selloff Monday — S&P 500 -1.9%, Nasdaq -2.5%, Dow -739pts (-1.4%); futures pointed further down into Tuesday (S&P futures -1.8%, Nasdaq 100 futures -2.6%) as AI-stock jitters persisted.
Markets: Nvidia fell another 4.1% Monday, market cap dropping below $3.8T; 10-year Treasury yield eased to 5.12% and crude slid ~3.8% to ~$85.

Companies: Nvidia reports Q3 earnings today after the close (~5pm ET) — first report since CEO Jensen Huang's resignation — guided to ~$108B revenue; board reportedly not considering reinstating Huang.
Companies: Tyson Foods jumped ~9% on an improved beef-business outlook; Home Depot and Walt Disney also report earnings today.

Companies: Growing 'AI bubble' worries — Axios/WSJ note AI infrastructure spend (~$7T projected through 2030) is outpacing forecast revenue (~$3.6T), with Anthropic's IPO terms and OpenAI's widening losses adding to valuation-reset concerns.

Macro/Policy: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh says the Fed's task force is gaming out how AI could reshape the economy and labor market; October retail sales data due today, with Fed's Musalem, Williams and Hammack also speaking.
Macro/Policy: Huang scandal is fueling bipartisan momentum for tighter chip-export restrictions to China and straining the Trump administration's alliance with Big Tech.
